idiom_name: effect algebra as data + one interpreter per execution strategy
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a closed set of operation values that carry only data, expose one pure smart constructor per operation so business code never performs effects while building the program, and let the program be an ordinary composable value (a fold, a list of steps, a free monad). Execution happens in an interpreter that is total over the algebra - a fold, natural transformation or switch that maps each operation to a target runtime - and the boundary runner pairs program and interpreter. Ship at least three interpreters: production, an in-memory/test one whose semantics mirror production, and a logging or dry-run one; add a replay or retrying interpreter when the program is stored. Where composition across several monads or stack safety is required, use the ecosystem's free-monad/effect library instead of hand-rolling the machinery; where no reification is needed at all, tagless-final is the lighter alternative.
code_sketch:
# algebra: effects as data
Op = Get(key) | Put(key, value) | Log(message)

# smart constructors build values, never execute
get = lambda key: Get(key)
put = lambda key, value: Put(key, value)

# program is a value: a list of described steps
program = [put("a", 1), get("a"), Log("done")]

run(program, production_interpreter)   # real store, real log
run(program, in_memory_interpreter)    # dict + list: assert without mocks
pitfalls: Executing while constructing: a constructor that performs the effect destroys the data property the whole pattern rests on.
Handling a missing operation case with a silent default (no-op or zero) instead of a failure, so new operations run with wrong semantics.
Not writing a test interpreter that mirrors production semantics - interpreter drift is the pattern's characteristic failure mode.
Interpreting deeply nested or generated programs recursively without trampolining or a depth bound.
Interpreter drift: test and production interpreters silently disagree on semantics (timing, failures, ordering) — counter with property-based test that compares both interpreters on random programs.
Free-monad heap allocation: each step is a heap-allocated suspension; for hot paths, compile the fold into a flat loop over a mutable state bundle instead of reifying every step as a data structure.

Serializing programs with function references: storing Call('fetchUser', userId) breaks if the function signature changes; keep operations fully self-describing (HTTP method, URL template, payload schema) rather than function pointers.

Forgetting to handle Pure/Return: a fold that only handles Suspend/FlatMapped may silently drop the final return value, producing wrong results in programs that return computed values rather than only performing side effects.
